restatement: Core should expose a single structured render contract that the API, the CLI and the n8n node all consume. render(template, data, options) returns {ok, output, messages, stats{chars, estTokens, sectionsOmitted, iterations}, diagnostics} and never throws for template or data problems: on failure it returns ok false, an empty output and the located error first. Alongside it come validate (no data needed), spec (blocks, filters, operators, limits, version, covering every filter the engine accepts), a dependency-free ceil(chars/4) estimator that a tokenEstimator option can replace, and analyze, which now reports required and per-block-kind counts. resolveTemplate keeps returning strings and throwing. The n8n node renders through the structured result, writes output to its configured field and turns failures into NodeOperationErrors that carry line and column. No runtime dependency is added, core gets no n8n imports or I/O, and the build and bin are prepared for api/ and cli/.
verification_plan: c1: read render and confirm the result shape on success and that every exit path for template and data problems returns ok false, output '' and a located diagnostic first, with no throw. Probe adversarial data (null data, cyclic objects, BigInt, non-array FOR targets, bad filter parameters, math on objects) and adversarial templates.
c1: confirm stats.iterations counts FOR iterations across nested loops and that chars and estTokens are computed on the final output.
c2: confirm validate uses no data, reports syntax errors and unknown filters as located errors, and does not report missing variables.
c3: confirm analyze adds required === !optional on every variable and a blocks count keyed by block kind, including nested blocks and an empty object when there are none.

c4: confirm spec returns version, blocks, filters, operators, limits equal to the defaults and syntax, and that its filter list matches the engine's applyFilter set rather than a list that can drift from it.
c5: confirm the default estimator is Math.ceil(len/4), that tokenEstimator replaces it and receives the output, and that neither adds a dependency.

c6/m1: confirm resolveTemplate is unchanged for passing templates (no diff in resolve.ts or the engine's output path), that it still throws named errors, and that limits options reach the lexer/parser/interpreter with limit-* codes.

c7: confirm the node calls render, writes result.output to outputField (default resolved_prompt kept), and throws NodeOperationError with the first diagnostic's message and '(line L, column C)'. Run the pre-existing node tests to confirm nothing regressed.
c8/m2: confirm package.json has no dependencies, bin maps template-resolver to dist/cli/index.js, and tsconfig include adds api/**/* and cli/**/*.
m3: grep the core diff for n8n imports and fs/http/process I/O.
Scope: confirm every changed file is inside files_scope and the manifest, and that no frozen test was edited.
Run the gate command and the full jest suite.

findings.title: render throws a raw TypeError for cyclic data in a strict FOR over a non-array value

serves.scenario: A data problem (a FOR target that is a cyclic object) escapes render as an uncaught native TypeError instead of ok false with a located type-error diagnostic, which breaks the 'never throws for template or data problems' contract. API, CLI and node callers would get a crash or 500 instead of a result.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c1: on a template or data error it does not throw)
findings.reproduction: const o = {}; o.self = o; render('{{FOR o AS x}}a{{END_FOR}}', { o }) throws 'TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON'. Verified by compiling core/src with tsc and calling render from node. The throw comes from JSON.stringify(iterable) while the interpreter builds its own TemplateError message (core/src/interpreter.ts:280). render then rethrows it because it is not a TemplateError (core/src/render.ts, 'if (!(error instanceof TemplateError)) throw error'). Smallest fix: build that message with the existing safe coercion (tryCoerceToString, which already catches stringify failures) instead of a bare JSON.stringify.

findings.title: render throws when data is null or not an object, because data conversion sits outside the try

serves.scenario: One contract for API, CLI and node: render(template, null) throws 'Cannot convert undefined or null to object' from Object.entries(data) before the try block, so a JS or CLI caller that passes JSON 'null' as data gets an exception. The contract reserves an invalid-input diagnostic code for exactly this case.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c1: data error does not throw)
findings.reproduction: render('${{x}}', null as any) throws TypeError 'Cannot convert undefined or null to object' (verified with compiled core). Smallest fix: move the Map construction into the try, or check that data is a non-null object and return ok false with an 'invalid-input' diagnostic at 1:1.

findings.title: spec's filter list is a hand-maintained copy beside applyFilter's switch, not derived from it

serves.scenario: A filter added to applyFilter but not to FILTERS would be missing from spec. It would also be rejected by analyze/validate as unknown-filter, because KNOWN_FILTERS now derives from FILTERS, while render accepts it. The frozen test pins a fixed fixture list, so it would not catch the divergence.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test
findings.reproduction: Add a 'case "upper"' to applyFilter only. spec().filters lacks it, validate('${{a | upper}}') reports unknown-filter, and render succeeds. Note for the lead: dispatching applyFilter from FILTERS, or asserting the two match in a test, would close it.
evidence: test:rr-spec: lists exactly the engine's filters
